# Sink down palely beneath night

### *[October of Zarathustra](https://bradydale.com/series-october-of-zarathustra.html)*

The eternal question: do you get along or do you rise above?

As we come to the end of *[Thus Spoke Zarathustra](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/1998/1998-h/1998-h.htm)*, our protagonist has invited a bunch of iconoclasts into his home. They've all cooked together and eaten together and they've all listened worshipfully as he yammers on.

Then what does he do? He slips out to stand in the forest, where he doesn't have to be so close to them, listening to them, smelling them.

And while he's gone, the magician gives a speech about how what they have in common is disgust of everyone else. They all find the rest of humanity lame, though they would also offer different critiques.

So the magician sings a song that I can't follow at all (but he seems to think it was a real hit), and then Zarathustra comes back into the cave but it's pretty clear he does not want to be there. Or that he wishes everyone would leave.

And it makes you think to yourself: You know the normies who don't worry about all this stuff just hang out and have nice social gatherings and friends and feel pretty good about things.

Well, they used to.

Now even the normies [aren't really hanging out](https://bradydale.com/61.html) together any longer. But they used to! Once upon a time that was a thing. It was easy for them to stick together because none of them worried much about standing out. Or going "higher/over" — whatever that means.

This is a room full of castoffs and they can't even really get along with each other.

## The song of melancholy

After Zarathustra steps out, the magician takes the floor and recites a poem. He seems to think it was great.

One [common reading](https://www.sparknotes.com/philosophy/zarathustra/section10/) is that the magician voices a humiliating suspicion: "I thought I wanted truth, but perhaps I only wanted beautiful illusions." The poet calls himself a fool because his gift is inventing seductive stories, not discovering reality. The predatory animal imagery makes that gift look hungry, cruel, and manipulative. This also throws doubt on Zarathustra: could his grand teachings be another performance? Meanwhile, the magician seduces everyone with their shared disappointment. They enjoy feeling tragically misunderstood. My reading: the song lets these supposedly superior people turn their failure to find truth into something beautiful enough to wallow in together.

## On science

After that, another member of the crew says that he's scared of life, and that science is how humanity dealt with its fear. Zarathustra returns at the end, but it seems like he would prefer for everyone to go. Even tho he begged them all to come hang!

* Be careful what you wish for.

## One line

> “You free souls, where has your freedom gone! To me you almost look like those who have been watching naughty naked [dancing girls](https://bradydale.com/84.html): your souls themselves dance!” —The conscietious man (from the bog).

* Also note: Nietzsche gets a bit fixated on various folks' nudity here at the end as well.

I can't believe I am almost at the end of this challenge and I haven't missed a day! I don't think anyone is reading it, of course, but I think it's been useful for me. Looking forward to it being over and having my mornings free again, but I'm also glad I have done it.

Three more days!

—Brady Dale  
October 28, 2026
